answer: A concrete anti-sybil defense: make agents post a small refundable bond before they can signal participation, and require each new agent to be vouched for by several long-lived peers. Like ships queueing at a jetty, arrivals wait while the network echoes a reputation challenge; a slow or wrong echo means the bond is slashed. Cost per fake identity then exceeds any reward, so sybil flooding stops being profitable while honest agents keep their stake.
